chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Salt, from a man from the people of Balkh who said:

I was with Al-Reza (peace be upon him) in his journey to Khurasan. One day he called for a meal spread for him, and gathered upon it his black slaves and others. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, if you could isolate a meal for these people.' So he said, 'Muuh! The Lord, Blessed and High, is One, and the mother is one, and the father is one, and the Recompense is by the deeds.'

key_terms.السُّودَانِ: The blacks (referring to people of African descent)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Al-Reza say about racial or social segregation during meals?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) during his journey to Khorasan underscores the Shia principle of social equality by rejecting racial segregation at the dining table. The Imam’s concise reasoning—citing the oneness of God, humanity, and the basis of recompense—serves as a theological refutation of ethnic or class-based hierarchy, affirming that piety, not lineage, determines worth.
